newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek watchdog commission gets tough on checks.
newsitem.headline: Greek watchdog commission gets tough on checks.

text.p: Greece's capital markets commission said on Monday that the problem with Delta Securities' alleged fraudulent trading emerged not because of lax controls, but as a result of tough supervision that started on November 1.

"The problem that erupted on the Athens bourse came about as a result of stricter supervision that went into effect November 1 based on law 2396," it said in a statement. "It did not come about because of lax contols as is widely presented by the press."

The commisssion said the incident of a member brokerage failing to meet payment to the clearing house was of limited concern. But the problem grew out of proportion because it exposed imperfections in the exchange's clearing procedures.
After talks with the brokers association (SMEHA) it announced the following measures:
Payment to the clearing house will henceforth take place with cash or cashiers cheques. This measure went into a effect last week, it said.
The exchange's supervisory authorities will continue systematic checks and will bar from trade member firms that owe securities to the clearing house who do not deliver on time.

The commission has asked the Bank of Greece to liberalise credit to brokerages. This would enable brokers to borrow funds to settle payment obligations with the clearing house, as well as fund stock purchases.
The clearing house will withhold cash payments to brokers when they are even one day late in the delivery of shares.
The commission will set an interim transaction limit for brokerages based on their share capital, it said.
